title: Handshake
description: The component/hello exchange: the engine says what protocol versions and grants it offers, the component says who it is, which interfaces it implements and what it contributes. The handshake is the only source of truth about a component's contributions — there is no manifest to agree with it (ADR 0012). See spec.md §3.2–3.3.

ComponentHello.title: ComponentHello
ComponentHello.description: Engine -> component, the first request on every component pipe.

component-protocol-versions.description: Component-protocol major versions the engine can speak, in preference order.

plan-grammar-versions.description: Deprecated: a component writes no plan (ADR 0100), so an engine sends no grammar and a component must not depend on one. It named the plan-grammar versions an engine read, so a component that contributed fragments could write one the engine read.

grants.description: What the component was actually granted, so it can fail its own handshake usefully rather than at first use (spec.md §3.2).

ComponentHelloResult.title: ComponentHelloResult
ComponentHelloResult.description: Component -> engine. Everything the engine indexes about a component comes from here.

component-protocol-version.description: The version the component selected from the engine's list.

interfaces.description: The interfaces this component implements. A component is a package, not a role, and may implement several (spec.md §2.1).

name.description: For a component, its identity and its namespace for contributed operators and actions (spec.md §2.4).

version.description: Semantic version. Only the major is contract-relevant; requirements compare against this, never against a tag (spec.md §2.3).

Capabilities.title: Capabilities
Capabilities.description: Open capability map, as protocol spec §5.3. Member names are an open vocabulary; each value is an object, '{}' when presence is the signal. Both sides ignore names they do not know.

PactPluginCapability.title: PactPluginCapability
PactPluginCapability.description: What a pact-plugins bridge's handshake says about the plugin it serves (spec.md §9.3.1, ADR 0109): the plugin, the bridge, and every entry of the plugin's catalogue, bridged or not. It is how the engine learns which bodies a plugin compares, from the plugin.

name.description: The plugin's name. The component is 'pact-plugin-<name>'.

version.description: The version of the plugin the bridge loaded, which is the component's.

interface-version.description: The plugin interface version its manifest declares.

PactPluginCatalogueEntry.title: PactPluginCatalogueEntry
PactPluginCatalogueEntry.description: One entry of a plugin's catalogue, as the plugin registered it.

type.description: The plugin driver's name for the entry's type.

content-types.description: For a content matcher or generator, the content types it claims: its 'content-types' value split at ';'. Each is a pattern, a regular expression anchored at both ends and matched against a media type's type and subtype with any suffix, parameters stripped, as pact-plugin-driver matches it.

action.description: The contributed action an entry the bridge serves is reached through: a content matcher's compare-contents, a content generator's generate-content, a transport's verdict. Absent for an entry it describes and does not serve.

kind.description: For a transport the bridge drives, the transport kind it contributes for it (spec.md §9.3.1, ADR 0111). Absent for one it describes and does not drive.

values.description: The entry's values, as the plugin registered them.

Contributions.title: Contributions
Contributions.description: What the component adds to the engine's vocabularies. Every declared operator, action and generator name MUST be namespaced with the component's own name; the engine checks that at load rather than at first use (spec.md §2.4).

kind.description: The transport kind this component serves. Open vocabulary.

content-slots.description: Which slots of which parts carry content — octets a content component encodes and decodes (spec.md §5.5) — as part name -> slot names. Every other slot carries a plain JSON value the engine passes through unencoded. Absent means no slot carries content.

exchange-parts.description: Which part starts an exchange and which answers it (spec.md §5.7): the names the engine reads instead of spelling any. HTTP's are 'request' and 'response'; a kind with no reply half names no 'answering' part. Every transport the engine serves or drives with declares them.

credential-members.description: Which members of which slots carry credentials (spec.md §5.8, ADR 0074), as part name -> slot name -> member names, compared ignoring ASCII case: the engine records their values as a placeholder in a contract, unless a session keeps them, and never repeats them in a report. HTTP's are the request's 'authorization', 'proxy-authorization' and 'cookie' headers and the response's 'set-cookie'. Absent means none.

outcome-slots.description: Which slots of which parts tell one exchange's outcome from another's (spec.md §5.10, ADR 0086), as part name -> slot names: a provider-shape recording keeps one entry per value of them, so an operation's answers of different kinds do not widen each other. HTTP's is the response's 'status'. Absent means none.

roles.description: Which roles it supports: 'serve' accepts inbound traffic, 'drive' initiates outbound (spec.md §5.1). A transport may support both.

media-type.description: A media type, or a 'type/*' pattern.

degradations.description: Distinctions this content type cannot express, declared rather than pretended (shape spec §4.2, spec.md §6.4).

substitutions.description: What a value operator means under this content type: a shape operator's name to one of this component's contributed actions, which the engine compiles where it would compile the operator's core action, with the same children, in a slot of this type this component decodes. Only value operators can be substituted: any, equality, type, string, number, integer, decimal, boolean, null, regex, datetime, date, time, include, semver, not-empty and any-of. A substitution for a structure, a modifier or content-type, or of an action the component does not contribute, or by a component that does not implement matcher, fails its load as component-invalid; an operator name the engine does not have is ignored (spec.md §6.3, ADR 0100).

path.description: Where the loss occurred, for a per-decode degradation. Absent on a statically declared one.

name.description: Namespaced plan action, e.g. 'json:parse' (plan grammar §4.1). An unnamespaced name is reserved for the specification forever.

lazy.description: Whether the action evaluates its children lazily (plan grammar §2.4). Laziness is declared, never incidental.

comparability.description: What a subsumption checker may do with this operator (shape spec §8, spec.md §7.5). Absent means opaque: yes on identity, unknown otherwise.

variant-facet.description: The facet name of the dimension this operator contributes, when it contributes one (spec.md §7.4). Absent means it contributes none, which is the common case.

name.description: Namespaced generator, referenced from a shape node's 'generator' member (shape spec §3.4).

produces.description: Advisory note on what the generator produces. The binding rule is not advisory: its output must be admitted by the shape it generates for (spec.md §7.3).

point.description: A lifecycle point from design 2.7's open vocabulary.

changes.description: Context members this hook may replace at this point. The engine applies only declared changes and rejects an undeclared one (spec.md §8.2). A hook that only observes declares none and can make none.
